Angle On Diameter

GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: a straight line joins A to B across a circle, and another point P sits on the edge.
How to play: Drag P around the circle, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show the names, the right-angle mark or the angle hint.
Look for the math

Drag P as far as you like around the circle. The angle at P never changes: it is always a quarter turn. Here is why that cannot fail.

A line through the middle

The line AB goes straight through the centre O, so it is a diameter of the circle. The three lengths OA = OB = OP are all radii, so they are equal. The radius OP is drawn when you pick "Angle hint".

Two isosceles triangles

Because OA = OP, triangle AOP is isosceles: its base angles obey ∠OAP = ∠APO. In triangle BOP, ∠OBP = ∠BPO for the same reason. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the two opposite inside angles added together, so ∠OAP + ∠APO = ∠BOP and ∠OBP + ∠BPO = ∠AOP. Since ∠OAP = ∠APO, this gives 2∠APO = ∠BOP; likewise 2∠BPO = ∠AOP.

Half a straight angle

A and B lie on opposite sides of O, so ∠AOP + ∠BOP = 180°. Adding the two doubled angles gives 2(∠APO + ∠BPO) = 180°, hence ∠APB = ∠APO + ∠BPO = 90°. This is Thales' theorem: an inscribed angle measures half the central angle over the same arc, and half of a straight angle is a right angle.

What the checks found

The logic test tries 600 positions of P, all round the circle (skipping only the two where P lands on A or B), and measures every angle independently with the law of cosines. At each one ∠APB = 90°, the three radii are equal, the two central angles add to 180°, and every step of the chase above holds to within a billionth. It also checks the converse: a point whose angle is right really does lie on the circle. The old cut-the-knot page cited below is an Outline Mathematics article that shows the same theorem with a GeoGebra figure rather than the Java applet; the picture and the options here follow the applet itself.

Try dragging P almost onto A or B: the angle at P stays a right angle right up to the end.
